description: THE REACTIVE LAYER. Every line here is gated on state the player actually created, and says nothing that is not already true in the world. Conditions are written as NAMES, never enum numbers. `{quest_title}` is resolved at speak-time from real quest data - never hand-name a quest here, because a renamed quest would turn the speaker into a liar. Weights are high (6-9) because a reaction is a rare line that has earned the right to win the roll on the day its state holds; anti-repeat in _filter_responses stops it becoming the only thing an NPC ever says. topic_type: 0=LOCAL_NEWS 1=RUMORS 2=PERSONAL 4=TRADE.

responses.text: You're the one who saw to {quest_title}. My cousin told it three different ways before I worked out it was the same story.
They're still chewing over {quest_title} at the well. Nobody's decided yet whether to be grateful or frightened of you.
I don't have much to say to someone who's done what you've done. {quest_title}, and the rest of it. I sell eggs.
Word came back about {quest_title} before you did. That's usually how it goes with the ones who finish things.
Between {earlier_quest_title} and {quest_title} you've had a busier season than the whole of this street.
My boy asks after you. He's got the whole of {quest_title} wrong and I've stopped correcting him.
I know your face from the reports. {quest_title} came across my captain's desk with your name on it and no complaints attached, which is rarer than you'd think.
You saved us a patrol with {quest_title}. That's a week of somebody's boots we got to keep.
Some of the lads think you're doing our job for us. I think you're doing the parts of it nobody pays us for.
Pass, then. Anyone who closed out {quest_title} isn't the sort I'm posted here to stop.
{quest_title}, and before that {earlier_quest_title}. A man could get suspicious of that much helpfulness. I'm choosing not to be.
Twenty years on this gate and the only names I remember are the ones on charges. Yours isn't on one. That's a compliment.
For the one who handled {quest_title}? I'll not pretend I haven't already worked out what your custom is worth to me.
The roads have been better since you took {quest_title} in hand. My carters have stopped charging me hazard money.
Half my trade is knowing who's about to be important. You've been on that list since {quest_title}.
I hear things before the criers do. {quest_title} reached me in three days, which for good news is quick.
You've a reputation now and reputations spend. Not here, mind - here you spend coin like everyone else - but out there.
{earlier_quest_title}. Then {quest_title}. At this rate I'll be telling people I knew you when you couldn't afford the good rope.
I hear what you did about {quest_title}. Deeds are prayers a person makes with their hands. Yours have been loud lately.
Two people lit candles here after {quest_title}. Neither of them said your name. They didn't need to.
You carry a great deal for someone with no order behind them. {quest_title} was not a small weight.
Be careful. A person who fixes everything begins to believe everything is theirs to fix. I have watched better than you break on that.
The temple keeps no ledger of favours, but if it did, {quest_title} would be entered in a good hand.
{earlier_quest_title} and now {quest_title}. Rest is also an obligation. You are not exempt from it.
Everyone knows your face now. Congratulations. In my trade that's called a problem.
{quest_title}. Very public. Very loud. Somebody was watching all of that and it wasn't only the grateful.
You're useful. I don't say that to many. Useful and known is a strange thing to be at once.
Word of {quest_title} got as far as the cellar rooms. We don't usually hear the good stories down there.
{earlier_quest_title}, {quest_title}. You keep finishing things. That's a habit, and habits are how people get read.
The clean ones get statues. The clever ones get old. Pick which you're after before someone picks for you.
I know who you run with. I'm not saying it out loud and I'd thank you to buy something and go.
My brother-in-law drives a cart on that road. That's all I'll say to you. That's all.
You want to know about my life? My life is quieter when men like you are somewhere else.
Nobody here will name you to the guard. That isn't loyalty. It's arithmetic.
Rumours? You are the rumour. Half this street changed its mind about travelling because of you.
I had a son on the roads. He came home. I don't know whether to thank you for that or spit.
I know exactly what you are. Nothing on paper yet. Give me one honest witness and there will be.
Keep walking. Whatever business you have here, have it fast and have it in daylight.
Talk about myself? To you? I'll talk about you. There's a camp that answers to somebody, and everyone knows who, and nobody can prove it.
Directions. Here's one: out. The gate you came in by, before the shift changes and you meet somebody less patient.
You'll notice I haven't drawn. That's discipline, not friendliness. Don't confuse the two.
I've buried two men off that road this year. When your day comes I'll not be gentle about it.
Full price. No haggling, no credit, and I'd rather you didn't linger where my regulars can see you.
I pay a toll on that road now. I know whose hand it ends in. Buy what you came for.
You'll find my prices high today. You'll find them high tomorrow. Consider it insurance I'm buying from myself.
Two of my drivers won't take the run any more. They didn't say why. They didn't have to.
Thirty years in this trade and I've never once refused a customer. I'm not starting now. But don't ask me to smile.
If a thing goes missing off this counter while you stand at it, I'll not be able to prove anything and we'll both know.
You built something out there. Most people who try that end in a ditch by the second month. You didn't.
Respect. Genuinely. The road crews were a shambles before you took them and now they're a business.
We work different sides of the same coin, you and I. Mine's quieter. Yours pays better and ends sooner.
Here's a rumour worth having: the guard know. They've known a while. They're waiting for one witness who'll stand up.
A camp is a lot of mouths. Mouths talk. That's the part nobody warns you about when they hand you the crown.
You need anything moved that shouldn't be seen moving, you know where I sit. That offer costs you nothing to remember.
I will not refuse you the door. I will not pretend I don't know what walks through it.
Men come to me at the end of that road and they all say the same sentence. I could recite yours now and save us both the years.
A widow sat where you're standing last month. Her husband drove a cart. I'll leave you to do that arithmetic yourself.
There is a way back. It is long and it is public and it costs you everything you took. That is the only honest version.
You want absolution the cheap way. Everyone does. It isn't sold here and it isn't sold anywhere.
Pray if you like. I'll not stop you and I'll not join you.
There's a price on you. I'm not the sort to collect it, but somebody on this street is.
Don't stand so close. If the guard come by I'd rather not be the one you were talking to.
I've nothing to tell you. Whatever you did, I'd rather hear it from the crier than from you.
The only rumour going is about you, and I'll not be the one repeating it to your face.
They read your name out at the post this morning. It's a small town. Everyone was listening.
Pay it off. Whatever it is. People here forget quick once a thing's settled and never if it isn't.
You've a bounty. You've a lot of nerve as well, walking up to me to make conversation about it.
State your business and be short. I'm one word from calling this in.
I don't give directions to people with prices on them. Find your own way.
The fine stands until it's paid. Pay it, serve it, or run - those are the three roads and there is no fourth.
My life? My life is easier when people like you settle up. That's the whole of it.
I'm not arresting you standing here in the open with witnesses. Don't read that as mercy. Read it as timing.
Coin on the counter first. I've had my fill of debts owed by people the guard are looking for.
I'll trade with you. I'll not be seen enjoying it. Nothing personal - it's my licence.
There's a notice with your name on it two doors down. Settle it and I'll go back to pretending I hadn't read it.
News? The news is you. It's been a slow week otherwise.
My hand's near the shutter cord and it'll stay there. Take that how you like.
I've been robbed twice and neither man was ever caught. So you'll forgive me if I'm short with the wanted.
You've a price on you. Sit down, then - you're better company than most of what comes through that door.
First bounty is the worst one. After that you learn which streets have long memories and which don't.
Pay it if you can afford it. A standing bounty is a rope somebody else is holding, and they get to choose the day.
Don't tell me what you did. I like you better as a stranger with a problem.
They're looking for you in this town specifically. Which means the next town over is having a much nicer week.
You're hunted now. Hunted men make bad decisions fast. Slow down.
Sanctuary is not a wall, and it is not free of a reckoning. But it is a door, and it is open.
Debt to the town is not debt to the gods, and neither is settled by the other. Pay both.
I heard your name read out. I did not enjoy hearing it.
Whatever you took, someone is short of it tonight. Start there and the rest gets simpler.
You are hunted. Hunted men come here at the end, not the beginning. Come at the beginning for once.
I will not name you to the guard. I will also not lie for you. Understand exactly what you have from me.
The dwarves held. They actually held. My grandfather said that hold would outlast us all and it looks like he was right after all.
They say a human went down into the deep levels with them. They say it like it's a story. I've stopped arguing.
There's dwarf iron in the market again. First time in two years. Whatever happened down south, it happened well.
My cousin sells to the passes. He came back with his cart empty and his purse full and a very strange look on his face.
Goblins came up out of the low caves and they went back down again. That's the whole story anyone here can tell you.
I never thought about the dwarves one way or the other until they nearly weren't there any more.
Dwarf steel's flowing again and my margins have never looked healthier. Whoever we owe for that, I hope somebody's buying them a drink.
The hold's buying grain again. Do you know what a hold under siege doesn't do? Buy grain.
Two years of no southern trade and then a caravan comes through the passes like nothing ever happened. I nearly wept over the manifest.
Prices came down when the hold held. I'm passing that on to you, which is not a sentence I say often.
I had written off every coin I had south of the passes. I have been writing it back on all week.
Ask me for a discount today. Just today. I'm in a mood to give one.
The hold held. That's one border I don't have to think about at night any more.
Nobody up here understands what a goblin tide does when it finishes with a mountain and comes looking for the next thing. I do.
We were told to expect refugees off the southern road. We got traders instead. I'll take that trade.
The captain cancelled the southern muster. Best order I've been given in a year.
They say a dwarf king's body came up out of the pits and got the rites it was owed. Soldiers care about that sort of thing more than you'd guess.
If you had a hand in the south, you've a friend on this gate. That's worth more than it sounds.
A king got his rites. Whatever else was won down there, that was the part that mattered.
The dwarves keep their own rites and I've never seen them. I'm told they are very long and very stubborn. It sounds about right.
A body left unburied is a wound that stays open. That one is closed now. Be glad of it, whatever it cost.
We lit a candle for the hold every night for two years. Last week we stopped, and it felt strange to stop.
There is a version of this where the hold fell and we heard about it in the spring. I think about that version.
You went south when going south was foolish. I have no coin for that and no rite for it either. Only this: I noticed.
The hold's gone. Overrun. Nobody says the word fallen out loud but that's the word.
There were dwarves through here last month with everything they owned on their backs. Nobody's seen one since.
My husband asks every night whether goblins come this far north. I say no. I don't know that I believe it.
Iron's doubled. Salt's doubled. Everything that came up through the passes has doubled or gone.
They held those mountains longer than there's been a kingdom up here. And then they didn't.
I keep thinking somebody could have gone south. Somebody with a sword and no sense. Somebody did not.
Every price on this counter went up when the hold went down and I've had that argument nine times today already.
No dwarf steel. Not at any price, not from me, not from anyone this side of the passes. That trade is finished.
I had three hundred in credit sitting in that hold. I'll not see a copper of it. Neither will anyone.
Buy your metal now. I'm serious. Whatever you think you'll need, buy it this season.
The southern road's a rumour now. Nobody drives it. Nobody insures anyone who drives it.
Thirty years I bought from those mountains. I knew the names of the men who weighed my ore. That's the part that sits badly.
The hold fell. Which means the thing that took it is done eating and looking north. Sleep well.
Double watches since the south went quiet. Nobody's said why out loud. Nobody needs to.
I've been asked to draw up what we'd do if goblins came up the pass road. I've been asked to do it quietly.
Dwarves came through with nothing. Soldiers walking like men who lost an argument with a mountain. I've not forgotten the look.
Somebody could have gone down there while it still stood. Nobody did. I include myself in that.
If you're going south, don't. That's not an order and I'd give it as one if I could.
A whole hold went into the dark and there was nobody to say the words over any of them. That is the part I cannot put down.
We say the rites here now, for people we never met, in a language they would not have used. It is not enough and it is what there is.
Do not ask me whether it could have gone otherwise. I have asked myself and I did not like the answer.
Their king was never buried. Whatever else was lost, start your grief there and you will understand the rest of it.
Refugees came and went. Some stayed. They do not come to this temple and I have stopped inviting them.
There is a kind of guilt that belongs to everyone who was busy elsewhere. I carry my share. Carry yours honestly and it weighs less.
The southern trade's dead, which means everything southern is worth four times what it was. Think about that before you sell anything.
Bad years are good years in my line. I'd rather they weren't. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.
Refugees with nothing turn into hands for hire inside a month. We've taken on four. None of them will talk about the hold.
The hold held, so the southern road's open, so there are caravans on it again. I'll say no more than that.
You went down there for people who'd never do the same for you. I don't understand it. I'm not mocking it.
Dwarf work's in the market again and half of it doesn't have papers. Draw your own conclusions and keep them to yourself.
You wear Gaela's bond. I can see it on you the way you'd see rain on a coat. Sit, then. You're not a stranger here.
The Green Lady's own. She asks for hands, not words - you'll have worked that out by now.
Sworn to Chronos. Then you already know I'm going to tell you that you're early, and that it doesn't help.
The Eternal Watcher keeps a longer ledger than any of us. You've put your name in it. That's not nothing.
Morthane's bond. People flinch when they hear that. I don't - somebody has to stand at the end of things.
You're sworn to the one nobody prays to until they need to. Come in. There's usually room.
Gaela's own, in my shop. My mother would have made you take the bread for nothing. I'm less holy than my mother, but I'll come down a little.
Everything green on this counter grew because of the harvest bond. Don't tell me a devotee is going to haggle over the price of turnips.
A Chronos devotee. Every hourglass I've ever sold went to one of you and every one of you haggled anyway.
Morthane's bond, is it. I'll serve you and I'll not ask what you needed the shovel for.
You're bonded to the harvest. My whole family owes their year to that. You'll get no rudeness from this house.
Sworn to Chronos. My uncle went that way. He got very calm and very hard to talk to.
Morthane's. Right. Well. Somebody has to do it and I'm glad it's not me. No offence meant.
You're Morthane's. We've had three of yours through this gate for the graveyard trouble and every one of them was worth ten of mine.
Harvest bond. Good. The ones who feed people tend not to be the ones I end up chasing.
You've moved up. I heard before you walked in - that's how you know it's real.
Rank means the fence stops rounding down on you. That's the only part of it anybody actually cares about.
Standing like yours opens doors that were never locked, only shut. Different thing entirely.
There's people who'd take a job off you now rather than the other way round. Be careful what you ask for out loud.
You've standing with my people. That's not sentiment - it's a discount, and you'll see it on the total.
You've done enough for this town that I'd take your word over most men's oath. Don't waste that.
You're one of ours now, whatever you were before. People here decided that between themselves.
This house owes you and I dislike owing. Ask for something so I can stop.
I know what you've done to mine. Your coin's as good as anyone's and that is the only reason we're speaking.
You've made enemies of my people and you're standing in front of one. Say what you came to say.
I know what you are to us. I'm not brave enough to say more than that, so I'll say nothing more.
You have set yourself against everything I serve. And still the door is open, because that is what the door is for.
You crossed people I answer to. I'm not going to do anything about it. Somebody will.
You told me a story once and I checked it. Everything you say to me now goes through that.
I've been lied to at this counter by you specifically. Cash. Every time. Forever.
You lied to me. I have forgiven it, which is not the same as having forgotten it, and you should know the difference.
You told me something that wasn't true. I've been turning it over since and I still don't know why you bothered.
You lied to me and I caught it. That's not the offence - the offence is that you were bad at it.
